GD Catalogue

Augments and Components

Usage tips:
Type “flat” before a stat name (e.g. “flat health”) to match only its flat value.
Type “%” before a stat name (e.g. “% health”) to match only its percentage value.

No items match those filters.
Source: .extracted/records/items/enchants/*.dbr (Augments), .extracted/records/items/enchants/runes/*.dbr (Runes — a subdirectory easy to miss with a non-recursive glob), and .extracted/records/items/materia/*.dbr (Components). Runes grant an active skill, shown with its own description and full cost/cooldown/range breakdown. Components are always “No Faction” (faction-agnostic crafting materials).

Pet Bonuses: items with a petBonusName field point at a separate linked record whose stats apply to your pets and summoned minions, not to you directly — easy to miss since they are not inline on the item’s own record. Shown as brass “Pet: ” chips.

Standing Required: from records/game/gamefactions.dbr reputation thresholds (Honored = 10,000 rep, Revered = 25,000 rep) cross-referenced against each faction’s own reward-tier text. Rule: the item’s own itemClassification decides it — Magical requires Honored; Rare, Epic and Legendary all require Revered, regardless of slot. Inferred from that classification→reward-tier pattern, not a value stored on the item.

Target Farmable Gear

Usage tips:
Type “flat” before a stat name (e.g. “flat health”) to match only its flat value.
Type “%” before a stat name (e.g. “% health”) to match only its percentage value.

No items match those filters.
Source: every itemClassification=Rare record under the equippable gear folders of .extracted/records/, merged with a community reference list of MI names and drop locations. Blueprint-craftable items are excluded by cross-referencing every artifactName=/forcedRandomArtifactName= in records/items/crafting/blueprints/**: there is no per-item “craftable” flag, so this cross-reference is the only reliable signal.

Item Level replaces the Faction facet here — MIs have no faction. Each name exists at several tiers; only the highest-level tier is kept, and the bracket is that tier’s level.

Found lines come from the community reference list, not from game data: .extracted/ contains no monster→item drop linkage at all. A “(?)” suffix marks a location filled in from a web search rather than that list.

Craftable and Vendor Gear

Usage tips:
Type “flat” before a stat name (e.g. “flat health”) to match only its flat value.
Type “%” before a stat name (e.g. “% health”) to match only its percentage value.

No items match those filters.
Two halves, one tab. Craftable (Blueprint) items come from .extracted/records/items/crafting/blueprints/ (armor/weapon/relic/faction/awakened/runes/other, including the awakened/ subfolders — easy to miss with a non-recursive scan) cross-referenced against the resulting gear/relic/rune records. Vendor Stock (Ready-made) items are finished equipment a faction vendor sells outright, with no blueprint and no crafting step, read from the same market tables — entries pointing straight at a records/items/faction/** record. Use the Acquisition filter to see either half alone; the two share no records and no item names.

Source line: “Faction Vendor – Blueprint” means the vendor sells the recipe; “Faction Vendor – Ready-made” means the vendor sells the item. Both come from records/creatures/npcs/merchants/factiontables/<faction>_<tier>_01.dbr’s marketStaticItems= field — the real per-reputation-tier stock list, and the only marketStaticItems= source anywhere in the tree. “Random Drop” means the blueprint file is referenced by a generic loot table under records/items/loottables/. A blank source means neither signal was found — likely a starter/quest-reward recipe or a non-faction blacksmith’s always-available stock, NOT necessarily “unobtainable.” No blueprint is both a faction-vendor item and a random drop (checked: 0 overlap).

Rarity is the highest-level blueprint tier per name on the craftable half, and the record’s own itemClassification on the vendor half. Rare on a vendor item does not mean Monster Infrequent — that reading only holds inside the gear folders the Target Farmable Gear tab scans, which never include records/items/faction/.

Faction potions (faction/booster/), consumables, and directly-sold augments and runes are excluded: the first two are not equipment, and the Augments and Components tab already carries the last two.
